title: Riser & Core Critical Quality Check
status: Draft for agreement with James Myers

location.areaHint: e.g. R2, ELV-1, Stair lobby riser

questions.q: Are drawings and tech subs at Status A, and is the benchmark for this riser type accepted?
Is the riser wall type and fire rating confirmed from the fire strategy (120 min to stair lobby risers, with an E60Sa door)?
Are floor channel fixings at ≤600 mm centres and head fixings at ≤300 mm, with 2 staggered rows for channels 94 mm and wider?
Is the first fixing no more than 50 mm from the track end, and is the head detail to British Gypsum spec with the correct stud gauge?
Is the deflection gap to the detail, with no conduit, cable or track inside it?
Are noggins and pattresses to the mark-up, mouse holes closed, and back boxes and conduits in?
Is the riser dry? If the envelope is still open, is FireLine MR or FireCase board being used?

sections.title: OPENINGS: BWIC AND RISER DOOR APERTURES

questions.q: Is each BWIC the correct size and position and lined to the fire-stopper's requirements, with any oversized hole pattressed?
Are there at least 50 mm from the services to the side and bottom of the opening, and at least 150 mm to the soffit at a deflection head?
Is the riser door opening sized to the door schedule within W -0/+10 mm and H -0/+5 mm?
Is there at least 200 mm of standard wall either side of and above the riser door frame, at least 300 mm between adjacent apertures, and an upstand of at least 100 mm?
Is a timber insert fitted on all 4 sides of the opening in a steel stud wall, unless Selo has confirmed it isn't needed for this shaft wall?
Is the dry riser cabinet opening built to suit the approved box?

sections.title: MEP 1st FIX: ALL SERVICES THROUGH OPENINGS

questions.q: Is the first support within 400 mm of the seal, or within 300 mm each side for Argus sprinkler pipe?
Are like services at least 50 mm apart, uninsulated metal pipes at least 100 mm apart, and the spacing within the tested detail?
Are services independently supported so no load sits on the seal?
Is the equipment approved and in its drawn position, with ladder or tray signed off and containment adequate?
Are the SWAs cleated, dressed, undamaged, at the correct bend radii, looming tidy, and secured with metal ties?
Is earth bonding complete, cable ends labelled, danger notices fitted, and access for maintenance adequate?
Is copex taken to the top of containment, with edge trim and unistrut end caps fitted?
Is there a signed pressure test certificate (1.5× working pressure, calibrated gauge) before insulation?
Can isolation valves still be operated once lagged, are drain cocks accessible and not buried, and is the insulation undamaged?
Are pipework IDs and flow direction labelled, and the riser clean?
Are vertical duct bearers Type A or B (RSA/RSC to span table) on fire-rated anchors?
Is each smoke or fire damper supported at every corner, fire stopped to the Mandik tested detail, with its actuator cover removable?
Has DW/143 leakage testing been done in all risers, and have the dampers been drop-tested?
Is the pipe 100 mm galvanised, with long-radius bends and brackets to the table (at least 1 within 1 m of each mechanical joint)?
Is the lowest point of the landing valve at least 750 mm above FFL, with "DRY RISER OUTLET" labelling and the pipe equipotentially bonded?
Is the air release valve above the highest landing valve, and are the isolation valves chained and padlocked open?
Has the test been done (air at 0.5 bar for 15 min, then water at 12 bar for 10 min), witnessed by MPX, with a permit to fill?
Is the outlet in its final orientation, the cabinet glass intact and correctly positioned, and the surround made good?
Are fire alarm cables on their own supports, using metal clips?
Is the cable testing recorded (circuit testing witnessed)?
Have MEA, the MEP trade and CLM all signed that the opening is ready?
Is CLM FIRAS-registered, with the correct fire rating confirmed against the fire strategy drawings?
Is the fire stopping to the tested detail, with the OneTrace record and seal label?
Where the riser meets a floating floor or the top of a void, has a detail been issued and the void fire stopped?
Is every penetration in an AV or ELV riser sealed, with no unsealed re-entry?
Has the MEP handover been received (HP), sockets and draw wires and putty pads fitted, and photos taken before closure?
Are boards fixed at the correct centres and staggered, mouse holes closed, and the wall within tolerance?
Is fire tape complete and the smoke seal taped and jointed?
Is the Selo Quadra+ or Ligna installed to BS EN 16034 by a third-party accredited installer?
Are frame gaps filled with intumescent acrylic as certified, and frame sealant joints formed?
Is the threshold level and square to the frame and leaf, with voids sealed?
Are smoke and acoustic seals fitted? Doors are Rw 35 dB for mechanical and public health, and Rw 30 dB for electrical.
Is the door label present (manufacturer, rating, serial), the FDKS sign fitted, and the lock and ironmongery to schedule?
Was the door fitted after wet trades had dried? Is third-party verification in place?
Is the grating the approved Blue Diamond GRP, cut to ±5 mm, clipped, with no rocking?
Are cut-outs around services neat, with no clash with supports or the ladder?
Is the roof riser opening weatherproofed with the approved Jones system, and the riser dry with no staining?
Are all services labelled: cables, pipes, ducts, dampers, dry riser and seals?
Is riser lighting working?
questions.source: Not found in the ITPs or tech subs. Confirm against the Borough spec

questions.q: Is the ladder or access in place, and are valves, dampers and isolators reachable?
Is the riser clean, with no swarf, offcuts or redundant rods, and all rods capped?
